description: Use this skill when writing Apex that must check governor limits at runtime before executing expensive operations — guard clauses, early-exit patterns, Queueable re-queue on limit approach, and batch scope sizing. Also covers building the monitoring layer above those checks: ApexTestResultLimits regression gates in CI, debug-log LIMIT_USAGE events, and a Scheduled Apex poller that writes OrgLimits readings into a Limit_Snapshot__c time series with threshold alerts. Trigger keywords: check governor limits before SOQL apex, defensive coding against limits apex, Limits.getDMLStatements getLimitDMLStatements, Limits class usage, guard clause governor limits, remaining SOQL queries Apex, heap size check before DML, LimitException handling, alert before we hit a governor limit, limit consumption regression in CI. NOT for diagnosing a limit you already hit — use apex/governor-limits. NOT for CPU and heap tuning — use apex/apex-cpu-and-heap-optimization. NOT for choosing which org limits matter or the org-wide alert routing architecture — use architect/org-limits-monitoring.
inputs: The Apex class, trigger, or batch class under review
Expected data volume or iteration count if batch/bulk
Whether the transaction runs synchronously or asynchronously
Which limits matter for this org (from architect/org-limits-monitoring, if that work has been done)
The degrade behaviour the business will accept when headroom runs out
name: apex-limits-monitoring
official_sources: Apex Developer Guide — Per-Transaction Apex Limits, `apexdev L19529–19660`: the sync/async ceiling table, the note that synchronous limits apply to scheduled Apex, the `getLimitAggregateQueries()` relationship-subquery footnote, the DML-statement counting list, and the CPU-time definition (Core Concepts sync/async table; Gotchas 2, 3, 8, 12).

Apex Developer Guide — Per-Transaction Certified Managed Package Limits, `apexdev L19664–19686`: separate per-namespace allocations and the 11× cumulative cross-namespace ceiling (Gotcha 5; the "does a managed package run here" question).
Apex Developer Guide — Exceptions that Can't be Caught, `apexdev L39718–39728`: `System.LimitException` is uncatchable and `finally` blocks do not run either (Gotcha 1; anti-patterns 1 and 2).

Apex Developer Guide — Using Limits, startTest and stopTest, `apexdev L41434–41455`: `startTest` adds a limit context rather than refreshing one, with the 98-query worked example (Gotcha 6; the test-shaping guidance).
Apex Developer Guide — Apex Stub API Limitations, `apexdev L42199–42213`: static methods and System types cannot be mocked (Gotcha 11; the `OrgLimitsPoller` injection seam and anti-pattern 7).

Apex Developer Guide — Transaction Finalizers, `apexdev L16290–16303`: synchronous limits apply to a Finalizer except for heap, `enqueueJob` count and `@future` calls (sync/async notes; the post-mortem surface table).

Apex Developer Guide — Debug Log Event Types, `apexdev L38274–38289`, `L38550–38562`, `L38925–38944`: the emitted `CUMULATIVE_LIMIT_USAGE` block and the documented `LIMIT_USAGE_FOR_NS` field list, including their level thresholds (Gotcha 5; the post-transaction horizon).

Apex Reference Guide — Limits Class, `apexrefguide L220152–221030`: the complete `getX()`/`getLimitX()` inventory, the "two versions of every method" statement, the "approximate" qualifier on `getHeapSize()`, and the reserved and deprecated entries (Core Concepts method table; Gotchas 7 and 10).

Apex Reference Guide — OrgLimit and OrgLimits Classes, `apexrefguide L226068–226260`: `getAll()`/`getMap()` signatures, `getName()`/`getValue()`/`getLimit()` semantics, the `toString()` sample, and the near-real-time update note (org-wide horizon; Gotcha 9).

Object Reference — ApexTestResultLimits, `object_reference L32556–32702`: the complete field set, the View Setup and Configuration requirement, and the three Usage conditions that make it return nothing (Gotcha 4; the CI regression gate).

Object Reference — EventLogFile and the ApexExecution / ApexUnexpectedException event types, `object_reference L112511–112549`, `L113130–113250`, `L114246–114290`: `EXCEPTION_CATEGORY` naming the breached meter, `NUMBER_SOQL_QUERIES` being cross-namespace, and the View Event Log Files permission (post-mortem surface table).

REST API Developer Guide — Limits resource and List Org Limits, `api_rest L1998–2200`, `L7790–8130`: the `Max`/`Remaining` response shape, the limit-key list, the five-minute accuracy statement, and the View Setup and Configuration requirement (Gotcha 9; the org-wide horizon).

Salesforce Well-Architected — Overview: <https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/well-architected/guide/overview.html> (pillar framing for Reliability, Performance Efficiency and Operational Excellence).
outputs: Guard clauses inserted before expensive operations (SOQL, DML, heap-intensive work)
Early-exit and re-queue logic for Queueable jobs nearing the CPU or SOQL ceiling
Batch scope-size recommendation derived from per-record limit projection
Observability log statements that report remaining limit headroom as a percentage
A deployable LimitGuard class, OrgLimitsPoller Schedulable, Limit_Snapshot__c object, Limit_Threshold__mdt config and test class
A CI query over ApexTestResultLimits that fails the build on a per-test-method limit regression
